4730958638666871404:
The Fourth Senior Sister was actually the Fifth Junior Sister, and Chi Qingqian was the youngest among the five disciples. A petite girl who spoke slowly and always trailed behind the elders, she seemed forever obedient. Everyone had forgotten that this very girl had sneaked out of the mountain at the age of seven to gather herbs and returned carrying a ten-year-old Ou Yanxi—the older Fifth Junior Brother.
Outsiders thought Chi Qingqian was taciturn, but in front of the Eldest Senior Brother, Second Senior Brother, and Third Senior Sister, she would often chatter endlessly. From astronomy and geography to ingredients and their properties, she loved sharing with her seniors, who would pause their tasks to listen attentively. Later, there was also a Junior Brother.
Perhaps because she had saved his life, he listened even more intently than the other three seniors. Yet he always seemed preoccupied, unwilling—or perhaps afraid—to ask questions. His best response was merely a smile.
The Master praised her as a genius with a photographic memory, but she knew this Junior Brother she had carried into the mountain was even more gifted. She wasn’t jealous, only often puzzled—why was there always an impenetrable mist shrouding this prodigious Junior Brother?
There were too many things she couldn’t understand. Why did the Third Senior Sister, who clearly liked the Second Senior Brother, refuse to say it?
And why did the Second Senior Brother, who also liked the Third Senior Sister, always brush it off with a frivolous demeanor, never earnest?
Was the Eldest Senior Brother a machine? Why did he never tire?
Why did the Master always pretend to be stern? Behind the scenes, he would beam with pride when mentioning his disciples to other Elders, his beard practically floating.
If the Master valued the Junior Brother’s talent the most, why wouldn’t he pass down the most profound techniques to him?
With so many fascinating things in the mountain, why did her seniors choose to betray and leave? Was Mohist Hill not good enough?
Too many mysteries—if she didn’t understand, she would ask.
As the mountain’s restrictions tightened, before departing, Chi Qingqian only visited her Junior Brother, locked in the Floating House. That night, saying goodbye through the door, he grew frantic for the first time, speaking endlessly and even releasing his mechanical venomous insects to try and sting her unconscious. But once Chi Qingqian made up her mind, no one could stop her—it had always been that way.
Over a decade ago, she had sneaked out and brought back a Junior Brother. This time, she left for answers about her seniors.
Later, she found all the answers. Sadly, she realized in the end that those answers didn’t belong to her.
During their final charge against the Enemy, standing side by side with her seniors, she suddenly recalled a face—earnest, listening, smiling warmly. If only none of them had ever left the mountain… how wonderful that would have been.
